questions.question: What is a fossil, and why are most fossils found in sedimentary rock?
questions.expected_answer: A fossil is the remains, such as bones, teeth, shells, wood or leaves, or a trace, such as a footprint, of a plant or animal that lived very long ago, preserved in rock. Most fossils are found in sedimentary rock because they form when dead plants and animals are buried in sediment like mud and sand, which later hardens into rock. Heat in rocks formed from melted rock would destroy them.

questions.question: Describe the steps in how a fossil forms.
questions.expected_answer: A plant or animal dies and is buried quickly by mud or sand, before it is eaten or rots away. Its soft parts rot, but hard parts like bones and teeth remain. More layers of sediment pile up and harden into rock. Water carrying minerals seeps through and slowly replaces the bone with stone in the same shape. Millions of years later, weathering and erosion uncover the fossil.

questions.question: Explain how fossils are a record of the history of life.
questions.expected_answer: Fossils show what plants and animals that lived long ago looked like, and many of them, like the dinosaurs, are now extinct. Fossils in deeper, older layers are different from those in younger layers above, which shows that life has changed over a very long time. Fossils can also show how places changed, such as sea shells found on land that was once under the sea.
